title: meridian-request-register/1
description: A field repository's request register, as read by Meridian's Product Owner. One file per field repository, in docs/requests/. The register is the field's half of the loop: it says what was asked for, what was delivered, what remains, and what the requester has answered. Additive properties are allowed everywhere on purpose — a field repository may carry its own columns (priority, effort, category) and a reader that ignores them loses nothing.

$schema.description: The identifier of this shape. It is a name, not a URL: the schema that defines it is docs/requests/register.schema.json in the Meridian repository.

source.description: Where the requests came from, and at which point of the field repository they were read.

remote.description: Clone URL, when it is not https://github.com/<repository> — a self-hosted forge, or a path in a test.

branch.description: The branch the requests were read on. The default branch is often not where the material lives.

commit.description: The commit read. The review script diffs the branch against it and names the files that moved.

documents.description: The documents of the field repository the round was read from.

branchPinned.description: The Meridian branch the field repository pins while no tag carries the work.

productOwner.description: Who answers, on Meridian's side, and under which charter.

charter.description: The document that appoints the Product Owner and states the duty.

command.description: The command that runs a round.

channel.description: How the two sides talk: where a request is answered, what the three acceptance states mean, and what happens on a disagreement.

issues.description: Where a request is answered — the issue tracker of the answering repository.

acceptance.description: The vocabulary of the three states a line passes through, written out so that a reader of the data never has to guess.

notAccepted.description: What `accepted: false` means — the requester could answer and has not.

cannotAnswerYet.description: What `accepted: null` means — the requester is not in a position to answer.

registerVersion.description: Increases on every round. The field repository's tooling diffs against the version it last read.

vocabulary.description: The identifiers the field repository uses in its own ledgers, as regular expressions without anchors. The review script reads them rather than knowing them: `request` ids name something that should become a request here, `context` ids (decisions, ADRs, pull requests) are listed for the reader and never counted as missing.

id.description: The id in THIS register (REQ-07). Ids of the field repository's own ledgers belong in `origin`.

origin.description: The field repository's own ids that this request answers — the join between the two ledgers.

version.description: The Meridian version that carries the work, or null while it is not delivered.

delivered.description: What was built, by path or by name. Empty while nothing is.

measure.description: The test or the gate that proves the claim. A `done` line without one is an opinion.

issue.description: The issue of the answering repository where this line is answered, when the requester opened one.

accepted.description: The requester's answer. true — they said so on the issue. false — they are in a position to answer and have not. null — they cannot answer yet: nothing is delivered, or they have said they cannot judge it until they adopt it. false and null are NOT the same statement; a silent user and a blocked one are different problems.

released.description: A version tag a third party can fetch carries the line.

answerToSource.description: What the field repository can close on its side, in its own vocabulary.

observed.description: What the field measured, in its words.

priority.description: The requester's recommendation, not a commitment.

effort.description: The requester's estimate: S = days, M = weeks, L = a release.

allOf.description: A line with nothing delivered cannot have been accepted or refused acceptance — there is nothing to try. E-9: `accepted: false` on an open line reads as silence when it is really absence.
A released line names the version that carries it.
